title: Evacuation modelling: RSET and ASET
summary: An evacuation is safe when the time people need (RSET) is less than the time available (ASET), with a margin. Pre-movement time is usually the biggest and most uncertain part.
outcomes: break RSET into detection, warning, pre-movement and movement
estimate movement time with the hydraulic method
explain why pre-movement time dominates and is uncertain
treat RSET as a distribution, not a single number
narration_en: Fire engineers ask a simple question: will everyone get out before conditions become dangerous? The time available, called ASET, comes from fire and smoke modelling. The time required, called RSET, is the sum of four parts: the time to detect the fire, the time to warn people, the pre-movement time while people notice, decide and gather their things or their families, and the movement time to walk to and through the exits. A design is acceptable when RSET is clearly shorter than ASET. Movement time can be estimated by hand with the hydraulic method: the walking time, or the time for the crowd to flow through the exits, whichever is longer. Simulators add detail. But the largest and most uncertain part is usually pre-movement. People finish their conversation, look for friends, or wait for confirmation. Experiments and real evacuations show long, skewed distributions of pre-movement times. That is why careful studies treat RSET not as one number but as a distribution, and look at its high percentiles.
narration_ar: يطرح مهندسو الحريق سؤالاً بسيطاً: هل سيخرج الجميع قبل أن تصبح الظروف خطرة؟ والوقت المتاح، ويسمى ASET، يأتي من نمذجة الحريق والدخان. أما الوقت المطلوب، ويسمى RSET، فهو مجموع أربعة أجزاء: زمن اكتشاف الحريق، وزمن تحذير الناس، وزمن ما قبل الحركة الذي يلاحظ فيه الناس ويقررون ويجمعون أغراضهم أو عائلاتهم، وزمن الحركة للمشي إلى المخارج وعبرها. ويكون التصميم مقبولاً عندما يكون RSET أقصر بوضوح من ASET. ويمكن تقدير زمن الحركة يدوياً بالطريقة الهيدروليكية: زمن المشي، أو زمن تدفق الحشد عبر المخارج، أيهما أطول. وتضيف المحاكيات مزيداً من التفاصيل. لكن الجزء الأكبر والأكثر غموضاً هو عادة زمن ما قبل الحركة. فالناس ينهون حديثهم، أو يبحثون عن أصدقائهم، أو ينتظرون التأكيد. وتُظهر التجارب وعمليات الإخلاء الحقيقية توزيعات طويلة ومنحرفة لأزمنة ما قبل الحركة. ولهذا تتعامل الدراسات الدقيقة مع RSET لا كرقم واحد بل كتوزيع، وتنظر إلى نسبه المئوية العليا.

diagram.title: RSET against ASET
diagram.caption: Four parts add up to the time people need; it must stay below the time conditions allow, with a margin.

nodes.label: Detection
nodes.detail: Time from ignition (or an incident) to detection, from detector design or fire modelling.

nodes.label: Warning
nodes.detail: Time to alert people: alarms, voice messages, staff. Voice messages work better than bells.

nodes.label: Pre-movement
nodes.detail: Recognition and response. Often the longest and most variable part; depends on alertness, familiarity, staff and message quality.

nodes.label: Movement
nodes.detail: Hydraulic estimate: max(walking time, people ÷ exit capacity), or a simulation.

nodes.label: RSET
nodes.detail: Required safe egress time = detection + warning + pre-movement + movement.

nodes.label: ASET
nodes.detail: Available safe egress time: until smoke, heat or toxicity become untenable, from fire modelling.

nodes.label: As a distribution
nodes.detail: Sample uncertain inputs (Monte Carlo) and compare high percentiles of RSET with ASET.

tour.text: First the fire must be detected and people warned.
Then people notice, decide and gather: pre-movement, often the longest part.
Then they walk and queue through the exits.
The four add up to RSET, which must stay below ASET with a margin.
Because the inputs are uncertain, treat RSET as a distribution.

sections.heading: Two clocks
sections.html:
Performance-based fire engineering compares two times. ASET, the available safe egress time, runs until smoke, heat or toxic gases make conditions untenable; it comes from fire modelling. RSET, the required safe egress time, is how long people need:

RSET = tdetection + twarning + tpre-movement + tmovement

The design is acceptable if RSET < ASET with an adequate safety margin (see the SFPE Handbook and PD 7974-6).

sections.heading: Movement time by hand
sections.html:
The hydraulic method takes the longer of walking time and flow time:

tmovement ≈ max( distance ÷ speed, people ÷ (specific flow × exit width) )

Example: 1,500 people, 6 m of exits at 1.3 per m per s, 60 m at 1.2 m/s: walking 50 s, flow 1,500 ÷ 7.8 ≈ 192 s, so movement ≈ 192 s. With detection 60 s, warning 30 s and pre-movement 120 s, RSET ≈ 402 s, about 6.7 minutes.

sections.heading: Pre-movement time
sections.html: People rarely move the moment an alarm sounds. They look for information, finish tasks, find their group. Measured pre-movement times are often long-tailed: most people start within a minute or two, some much later. Pre-movement depends on alertness (asleep or awake), familiarity, staff behaviour and the alarm: voice messages that say what to do shorten it compared with bells.

sections.heading: RSET as a distribution
sections.html: Uncertain inputs make RSET uncertain. Sample them many times (Monte Carlo): in the lab, a lognormal pre-movement around 120 s and uncertain flow and speed give RSET percentiles of about 323 s (5th), 409 s (50th) and 569 s (95th). Compare a high percentile, not the average, with ASET, and report how sensitive the result is to each input.

callouts.title: Explore it
callouts.html: In the explorer, double the pre-movement time. Then double the exit width instead. Which changes RSET more?

callouts.title: Zero pre-movement
callouts.html: Simulations that start everyone moving at time zero can underestimate RSET badly. Always add a realistic pre-movement distribution.

explorer.intro: Set each part of RSET and the ASET from fire modelling.
explorer.predict: Which usually changes RSET more: pre-movement time or exit width?

code.title: RSET and its uncertainty
code.explain: A deterministic hydraulic RSET, then 5,000 Monte Carlo samples of uncertain pre-movement, flow and speed.
code.expected:
deterministic RSET: 402 s
RSET 5th / 50th / 95th percentile: 323 / 409 / 569 s; ASET 900 s
share of runs with RSET > ASET: 0.0%

takeaways: RSET = detection + warning + pre-movement + movement; it must be below ASET with a margin.

Pre-movement time is often the largest and most uncertain part.
Treat RSET as a distribution and compare high percentiles with ASET.

glossary.def: Required safe egress time: detection + warning + pre-movement + movement.
Available safe egress time, until conditions become untenable.
Time from warning to the start of purposeful movement.
Movement time from flow rates and walking speeds.
Repeated random sampling of uncertain inputs to get a distribution of results.
